title: Add benchmark-lab adaptive-batching profiling and reporting pipeline v90
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Add adaptive-batching profiling baselines and a new reporting pipeline to produce per-variant latency/cost distributions for autoscaler and SLO tuning.
description:
Context and motivation: The benchmark lab needs better signal for adaptive batching and autoscaler tuning. Current profiling baselines do not capture tail latency behavior across mixed workloads or the interactions between KV-cache hit rates and batching heuristics. This PR adds representative workload runners for adaptive batching, new profiling baselines that capture cold/warm start regimes, and a reporting pipeline that aggregates latency/cost distributions per model/variant/sequence-length bucket.

What changed: Added a new adaptive batching runner, updated workload generators to include chat-like and multi-turn conversational traces, introduced profiling baselines for cold start and steady-state, and wired up a reporting pipeline that produces consolidated CSV/Parquet outputs and a daily dashboard ingestion job. Also added docs and quickstart for running baselines locally and in CI.

Highlights: - representative workload runners for adaptive-batching experiments - profiling baselines (cold/warm/steady) with standardized histograms and p99/p999 metrics - reporting pipeline that tags outputs by model-variant, quantization profile, and hardware target - CI job that runs a lightweight smoke profile on PRs and a scheduled daily job for full baselines

Checklist: - [x] add adaptive batching runner and tests - [x] add profiling baseline scripts and example configs - [x] add reporting ETL to benchmark-lab/pipelines - [x] add CI smoke job and nightly scheduled workflow - [x] update benchmark-lab README and runbook - [x] get reviewers' sign-off

Migration notes: Existing baseline consumers should be able to consume the new reporting outputs; the new pipeline writes a compatibility CSV and Parquet with the same keys plus additional columns for batching metadata. No runtime changes required for serving.

Related: ENG-4321 (adaptive batching experiments), ENG-4490 (autoscaler tuning), SUP-2143 (customer-reported perf variance).
